text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up: several customers asked today for a smaller onprem package that can be deployed in tightly restricted networks. want to outline a pragmatic MVP.
Mira Patel: Agree. Propose we split into two deliverables: a "lite" runtime (minimal control plane) and a formal airgap bundle (full asset tarball + hashes).
Samir Khan: Lite runtime: strip optional agents, telemetry, and admin UI. runtime binary stays the same as hosted to avoid model drift. aim: <50% control-plane footprint.
Nia Rivera: Airgap bundle must include signed manifests, SBOM, and a verification script. customers with HSM want guidance for provisioning KMS keys offline.
Raul Gomez: Upgrade story is the main fear. If someone installs lite, they need a non-destructive path to rolling upgrades later. suggestion: include a one-shot "expand" command that pulls missing components and migrates configs.
Kathy Li: We should be explicit in docs: lite = supported for single-node/short-lived installs. recommend full distro for HA clusters. Decision tree in docs.
Jason Park: Field note: support teams get tickets when customers install lite and later want HA. we need a clear FAQ + support playbook.
Alex Chen: Launch criteria proposal: 1) automated install finishes in <30m on an isolated VM, 2) upgrade converter tested v1.0-lite -> v1.0-full and v1.0-full -> v1.1-full, 3) security checklist validated by SRE.
Mira Patel: OKR idea: ship lite + airgap pilot with 2 regulated customers this quarter. that keeps scope tight.
Samir Khan: Rough estimate: control-plane slimming (2 sprints), installer + airgap tooling (1 sprint), converter + upgrade tests (1 sprint), pilot support (1 sprint). total ~5 sprints.
Nia Rivera: Security checklist (I): artifact signing, deterministic hashes, offline key rotation docs, ephemeral admin token generator. I'll draft a checklist and a verifier script.
Raul Gomez: Ops feature request: tiny network validator that verifies egress whitelist and can output a minimal routing diagram. I'll prototype a spike.
Kathy Li: Docs UX: create a short flowchart: choose lite vs full -> installer steps -> upgrade path -> rollback. include template customer comms for conversion maintenance window.
Alex Chen: Risks: fragmentation, more channels to support, and upgrade regressions. Mitigation: strict CI matrix and deprecation policy (lite supported for N months).
Jason Park: Also add telemetry opt-in flow so we don't lose critical debug signals by default. maybe allow secure upload to a customer-controlled S3 endpoint.
Samir Khan: Implementation note: keep the same model-serving runtime image tag; only change control plane images. makes compatibility easier.
Mira Patel: Action owners: Samir = tech spec for installer & converter (due 6d), Nia = security checklist + verifier (7d), Raul = network validator spike (2w), Kathy = docs decision tree + support playbook (9d), Jason = telemetry opt-in pattern (8d).
deploy-bot: Created epic PRIV-ONPRE-LITE and linked this thread.
Alex Chen: Great. we'll treat pilot customers as gating for GA. keep the scope narrow. schedule a 30m follow-up after Samir posts spec. :calendar: :thumbsup:
Kathy Li: I'll draft the decision tree and a short FAQ template this week.
Nia Rivera: I'll put the verifier script in the repo as an executable and add tests for hash checking.
Raul Gomez: Spike channel: #pkg-spikes. will share prototype and short demo there.
Samir Khan: I'll upload the initial spec to the epic by EOD Friday and tag eng-runtime + eng-platform.
Alex Chen: Thanks all. focus on low friction installs and an unambiguous upgrade story.
